question: The popular style of temple architecture in northern India is called ________.
solution:
Correct Answer **Nagara**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Northern India saw a rise in the popularity of temple architecture in the Nagara style.
 
• It typically lacks ornate boundary walls or entrances.
 
• The tallest tower is always exactly beneath the garbhagriha.
 
• There is an installation of Amalaka or Kalash on Shikhara.
 
• Nagara temples can be divided into many different types according to the shikhara's shape:
 
 
• Valabhi: Temples built in the Valabhi style are rectangular and have barrel-vaulted roofs.
 
• Wagon vaulted buildings and constructions get their name from having a vaulted chamber roof.
 
• Phamsana: These are shorter, but wider constructions made comprised of roofs with multiple slabs that rise up in a gradual slope on a straight incline like a pyramid meeting at one point over the middle of the building.
 
• Rekha-Prasad: A straightforward Shikara with a square base and inwardly curved walls with a pointed top distinguish Rekha-Prasad or Latina temples.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The Pallavas ruled over parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and northern Tamil Nadu until the ninth century.
 
• They are credited with developing the Dravidian style of temple architecture in South India.
 
• A compound wall encloses the Dravida temple.
 
• A Gopuram, or entrance doorway, is located in the middle of the front wall.
 
• The vimana, or main temple tower, is shaped like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The word "shikhara" is only used to refer to the crowning part at the top of South Indian temples.
 
• It is typically formed like a tiny stupika or an octagonal cupola.
 
• The garbhagriha's entrance is adorned with ferocious Dvarapalas, or the doorkeepers guarding the temple.
 
• A sizable water tank is frequently found encased within the complex.
 
• There are divisions among Dravida temples. These are basically five different shapes:
 
 
• square, kuta, and also caturasra.
 
• rectangular or shala or ayatasra.
 
• elliptical, coming from wagon vaulted shapes of apsidal chaityas with a horseshoe-shaped entry facade typically known as a nasi, also known as elephant-backed or vrittayata.
 
• circular or vritta.
 
• either ashtasra or octagonal.
